gen-dafont-arkhip-fs-nunito: Arkhip spaces its letters wide apart, with a gently opened c. Nunito, a rounder sans-serif, has the taller lowercase and soft terminals, so the heading does the geometric shouting and the body does the friendly talking.
gen-dafont-arkhip-fs-pilcrow-rounded: Pilcrow Rounded packs its letters tight, with big counters and curves that never quite close. Arkhip works the other way, floating its letters apart in a moderate lowercase, while Pilcrow Rounded stays warm as a sans-serif body.
gen-dafont-arkhip-fs-quicksand: Quicksand blows its lowercase up like glass bulbs, round and tall. Arkhip sits above in a lower, geometric display, and the two trade a floating, widely spaced headline for a plain sans body of identical bar thickness.
gen-dafont-arkhip-gf-aleo: Arkhip lets a wire-smooth line glide under the eye, every letter floating apart from its neighbor. Aleo, a dignified serif, takes over for the reading, with counters that invite the eye in.
gen-dafont-arkhip-gf-almendra-sc: Authoritative is the mood Almendra SC brings, with mouths that stay open on c, e and a. Beneath that, Arkhip's ruler-straight, modern strokes give the page a crisp geometric top against a lower, text serif body.
gen-dafont-arkhip-gf-antic-slab: Arkhip's strokes never swell or thin, and its letters float well apart in a modern geometric way. Antic Slab follows with round bowls and wide s curves, a classic serif body that gives the editorial side some weight.
gen-dafont-arkhip-gf-arvo: Traditional dignity belongs to Arvo, whose curves refuse to close, while Arkhip is the modern one, its stroke held at fixed pressure. Arkhip is best loud and geometric up top, and Arvo is best as a text serif body below.
gen-dafont-arkhip-gf-belgrano: Belgrano is classic and traditional, a text serif with open-mouthed curves that stay clear, set against Arkhip's counters outlined by one steady thickness. The strongest quality here is the old and new facing off.
gen-dafont-arkhip-gf-biorhyme: BioRhyme reads bookish and refined, its curve ends stopping like brush strokes lifted early. Over a longer stretch, this text serif keeps widely spaced capitals and a low profile, while Arkhip's flat, unmodulated strokes stay up top as the display voice.
gen-dafont-arkhip-gf-biorhyme-expanded: BioRhyme Expanded is a refined, bookish classic serif whose open gaps break each word into single letters, under Arkhip's heading of one unchanging stroke width. The strongest quality is that wide, spaced-out feel.
